title: Why Letters to Canada Get Returned or Delayed
description: Incomplete addresses, short postage and no return address: the reasons Canada Post lists for returning mail, and a checklist for letters from abroad.
keywords: why was my letter returned to sender canada post
answer: Canada Post lists an insufficient or nonexistent address, a move with no forwarding address, a refusal and insufficient postage among the reasons mail is undeliverable. It returns an item only when a valid return address is on it. Items from other countries go back to the country-of-origin undeliverable mail office. Check four things before you post.

ul: **The address is insufficient or does not exist.**
**The addressee has moved** and left no forwarding address.
**The item has insufficient postage,** or needs new postage before it can go. See [what happens with too little postage](/blog/letter-with-too-little-postage).

blocks.p: Sending the item back is a separate step with its own condition: Canada Post returns it only if it carries a valid return address. Without one it opens the item, and an item with no obvious value is destroyed.

sections.h2: A pre-flight checklist for a letter from abroad

ol: **Address in Canadian order,** ending in municipality, province and postal code: [how to address a letter to Canada](/blog/how-to-address-a-letter-to-canada).
**A correct postal code.** A missing or incorrect one moves the item to higher Lettermail rates: [Canadian postal code format](/blog/canadian-postal-code-format).
**Enough postage for the weight,** using your own postal service's international rate, or none if the letter is stamped in Canada.
**A return address** that can receive mail.

blocks.p: Canada Post's Lettermail delivery standards are estimates and are not guaranteed, and ordinary mail has no tracking. See [how long a letter takes in Canada](/blog/how-long-does-a-letter-take-in-canada).
